description: Martin Luther King Jr. Day is an American federal holiday honoring the birthday and transformative civil rights legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Observed annually on the third Monday of January, the holiday pays tribute to Dr. King's relentless advocacy for racial equality, justice, and nonviolent social activism.

First signed into federal law by President Ronald Reagan in 1983 and officially observed nationwide in 1986, MLK Day is also designated by Congress as a National Day of Service ('A Day On, Not a Day Off'). Across the country, millions of citizens participate in volunteer community service projects, lectures, and educational forums.
In 2026, MLK Day is observed on Monday, January 19, creating a standard three-day weekend for public schools, civil servants, and millions of workers across the nation.

name: Groundhog Day 2026
description: Groundhog Day is an iconic North American folkloric tradition celebrated every year on February 2nd. According to legend, if a groundhog emerging from its burrow sees its shadow due to clear weather, it retreats back inside, portending six more weeks of winter weather; if it does not see its shadow, spring will arrive early.

The largest and most famous ceremony takes place in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, where the legendary groundhog Punxsutawney Phil delivers his weather forecast from Gobbler's Knob before tens of thousands of enthusiastic spectators. The tradition evolved from ancient European Candlemas customs and German immigrant folklore.

In 2026, Groundhog Day lands on a Monday. Whether you are eagerly awaiting warmer spring temperatures or embracing late-winter activities, tracking the countdown gives a fun seasonal benchmark halfway between the winter solstice and spring equinox.

faqs.answer: Groundhog Day 2026 is on Monday, February 2, 2026.

faqs.question: Is Groundhog Day a public holiday?
faqs.answer: No, Groundhog Day is a popular cultural observance and not a federal or state holiday, so businesses, banks, and schools operate on normal hours.

faqs.question: Where does the Groundhog Day tradition come from?
faqs.answer: It originated from ancient European Christian Candlemas weather traditions, popularized in North America by German settlers in Pennsylvania in the 1880s.

name: Presidents' Day 2026
description: Presidents' Day, officially recognized by the federal government as Washington's Birthday, is celebrated on the third Monday of February. Established in 1885 to honor the nation's first president, George Washington, the holiday has evolved to celebrate all past American presidents, with particular emphasis on George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.

The date was shifted from Washington's actual birthday (February 22) to the third Monday of February under the 1968 Uniform Monday Holiday Act, establishing a reliable three-day weekend. It has also become a major retail event known for automobile, home appliance, and mattress sales.
In 2026, Presidents' Day takes place on Monday, February 16. It provides federal workers, stock traders, and students with a mid-winter long weekend.

faqs.answer: Presidents' Day 2026 is celebrated on Monday, February 16, 2026.

faqs.answer: Federal courts, the US Postal Service, public schools, and the New York Stock Exchange are closed on Presidents' Day.

faqs.answer: In federal statute (5 U.S.C. 6103), the holiday remains designated as 'Washington's Birthday', though many states and communities also commemorate Abraham Lincoln.

description: St. Patrick's Day is celebrated annually on March 17th to commemorate Saint Patrick, the patron saint of Ireland, and the arrival of Christianity in Ireland. Over centuries, it has transformed into a global celebration of Irish culture, heritage, music, dance, and gastronomy.

name: First Day of Spring (Spring Equinox) 2026
description: The Spring Equinox (Vernal Equinox) marks the astronomical beginning of spring in the Northern Hemisphere. On this day, the sun crosses the celestial equator from south to north, resulting in roughly equal lengths of day and night across the globe.

Historically, the equinox has represented rebirth, renewal, and agricultural planting across diverse ancient cultures, inspiring festivals such as Nowruz, Ostara, and Passover. In modern times, it heralds warmer temperatures, longer daylight hours, and the blooming of nature.
In 2026, the first day of spring arrives on Friday, March 20. Gardeners, outdoor enthusiasts, and seasonal planners use this countdown to prepare for planting and outdoor sports.

faqs.question: When is the first day of spring in 2026?
faqs.answer: In 2026, astronomical spring begins on Friday, March 20, 2026.

faqs.question: What happens on the Spring Equinox?
faqs.answer: The Earth's axis tilts neither toward nor away from the sun, giving nearly 12 hours of daylight and 12 hours of darkness everywhere on Earth.

faqs.question: Is astronomical spring different from meteorological spring?
faqs.answer: Yes, meteorological spring begins predictably on March 1 every year based on temperature cycles, while astronomical spring depends on the sun's position.

description: Easter Sunday is the Christian holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, described in the New Testament as occurring on the third day following his crucifixion. It is the culmination of Holy Week, following Lent, Palm Sunday, and Good Friday.

Unlike fixed-date holidays, Easter is a 'movable feast' calculated as the first Sunday after the first full moon (the Paschal Full Moon) occurring on or after the vernal equinox. In addition to church services, common family traditions include decorating Easter eggs, organizing egg hunts, and sharing springtime festive brunches.
In 2026, Easter Sunday will be celebrated on Sunday, April 5. Tracking the days left is helpful for booking spring travel and preparing family gatherings.

faqs.question: Why does the date of Easter change every year?
faqs.answer: Easter is determined by a lunisolar calendar formula established at the Council of Nicaea in 325 AD: the first Sunday following the full moon on or after March 21.

name: Juneteenth 2026
description: Juneteenth (officially Juneteenth National Independence Day) is a US federal holiday celebrated on June 19th. It commemorates the day in 1865 when Union Major General Gordon Granger arrived in Galveston, Texas, enforcing General Order No. 3 and declaring that all enslaved people were free—more than two years after President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

Also known as Freedom Day, Jubilee Day, and Black Independence Day, Juneteenth is the longest-running African American holiday. In 2021, President Joe Biden signed the Juneteenth National Independence Day Act, making it the 11th officially recognized US federal holiday.
In 2026, Juneteenth falls on a Friday. Across the country, communities celebrate with educational symposiums, parades, street festivals, barbecues, and family reunions.

faqs.answer: Yes, as an official US federal holiday, post offices, national banks, federal agencies, and federal courts are closed.

faqs.answer: The name is a portmanteau of the words 'June' and 'nineteenth', commemorating June 19, 1865.

name: First Day of Summer (Summer Solstice) 2026
description: The Summer Solstice is the astronomical start of summer in the Northern Hemisphere and the longest day (with the most daylight hours) of the entire calendar year. It occurs when Earth's geographic pole reaches its maximum tilt toward the sun (approximately 23.4 degrees).

For thousands of years, civilizations have celebrated the summer solstice with festivals, bonfires, and gatherings at ancient celestial monuments like Stonehenge. In modern life, it signals the height of outdoor recreation, beach trips, and warm summer weather.
In 2026, the summer solstice occurs on Sunday, June 21. Use our countdown calculator to see the exact number of days remaining until the sun reaches its highest point in the sky.

faqs.answer: The summer solstice in 2026 occurs on Sunday, June 21, 2026.

faqs.question: Why is the summer solstice the longest day of the year?
faqs.answer: Because the Northern Hemisphere is tilted closest to the sun, allowing the sun to travel its highest and longest path across the sky.

faqs.question: Do daylight hours get shorter after the summer solstice?
faqs.answer: Yes, starting the day after the solstice, daily daylight hours gradually decrease until the winter solstice in December.
